title: Conjunctions, Combustion and Retrogression
subtitle: Understanding shared planetary placement, solar proximity and apparent backward motion without simplistic labels
summary: This session explains three frequently misunderstood planetary conditions: conjunction, combustion and retrogression. Students learn how planets sharing a sign or house interact, why degree distance matters, how close proximity to the Sun may modify a planet's expression, and why retrograde motion does not automatically make a planet weak, negative or unusually strong. The session provides a disciplined sequence for combining these conditions with dignity, house placement, lordship, aspects and Dasha timing.
learningObjectives: Define planetary conjunction in sign-based and house-based chart reading.
Explain why degree distance changes the intensity of a conjunction.
Identify the difference between a dominant planet and a supporting planet within a conjunction.
Explain combustion as close proximity to the Sun.
Avoid treating every combust planet as completely powerless.
Explain retrogression as apparent backward motion from Earth's viewpoint.
Avoid assuming that every retrograde planet is automatically weak, strong or negative.
Combine conjunction, combustion and retrogression with dignity, lordship, aspects and timing.
prerequisites: Completion of Session 13: Planetary Aspects — Graha Drishti.
Knowledge of planetary dignity, relationships, houses, house lords and aspects.

keyTerms.meaning: Two or more planets occupying the same sign or house.
keyTerms.note: Their interaction must be judged by degree distance, strength, dignity, lordship and natural relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: The angular separation between two planets within a sign.
keyTerms.note: Closer planets generally interact more intensely than widely separated planets.

keyTerms.meaning: The relative ability of one planet in a conjunction to express its agenda more strongly.
keyTerms.note: Dominance may depend on dignity, degree position, natural strength, lordship and condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition in which a planet is very close to the Sun and its independent expression may be reduced or altered.
keyTerms.note: Exact limits vary by planet, tradition and calculation standard.

keyTerms.meaning: The apparent backward motion of a planet as seen from Earth.
keyTerms.note: Retrogression changes expression and emphasis; it should not receive a single universal label.

keyTerms.meaning: Motion as observed from Earth rather than the planet literally reversing its orbit.
keyTerms.note: Retrograde motion is an observational effect caused by relative planetary movement.

keyTerms.meaning: A factor that modifies how a planet expresses its promise without replacing the complete chart judgement.
keyTerms.note: Combustion and retrogression should be used as modifiers, not isolated verdicts.

blocks.text: A conjunction occurs when two or more planets occupy the same sign or house. Their agendas meet in one location, but they do not merge into a single planet. Each planet retains its own nature, lordship, dignity, strength and role while interacting with the others.

blocks.altText: A simple comparison of close and wide planetary conjunctions within the same sign.
blocks.caption: Same sign does not always mean equal interaction intensity.
blocks.purpose: Introduce conjunction and the importance of degree distance.

blocks.title: A conjunction is a relationship, not a verdict
blocks.text: The presence of two planets together does not by itself prove success, failure, Yoga, Dosha or a specific event.

Two planets may occupy the same sign but remain far apart by degree. A close conjunction usually produces stronger interaction, while a wide conjunction may behave more like shared sign occupancy with weaker direct blending. Exact interpretation depends on the planets and the method used.

left.label: Close conjunction
points: One planet may dominate or strongly modify the other.
Requires careful check for combustion or planetary war where applicable.

right.label: Wide conjunction
points: Large degree separation within the same sign.
Shared house and sign themes remain.
Other aspects and conditions may become more important.

blocks.title: Same sign, different intensity
blocks.scenario: Mercury and Venus are in the same sign in two charts.
steps: In the first chart they are separated by two degrees.
In the second chart they are separated by twenty degrees.
Both charts show conjunction by sign.
The first chart usually requires stronger interaction analysis than the second.
blocks.conclusion: Always record degree distance before describing conjunction intensity.

blocks.caption: Factors that may influence planetary dominance
rows: Which planet is in a stronger sign condition?
Which planet has stronger functional importance for the Lagna?
Which planet is more tightly connected to the other?
Does one planet naturally express more forcefully in this context?
Is one planet too close to the Sun?
Which planet receives stronger support or pressure?
blocks.note: Dominance is contextual and should not be assigned from one factor alone.

blocks.title: Dominant and supporting roles
blocks.scenario: Two planets occupy the tenth house.
steps: Identify the houses owned by both planets.
Compare their dignity and degree positions.
Check conjunction distance and aspects received.
Identify which planet is active by Dasha.
Describe one as more dominant only if multiple factors support that conclusion.
blocks.conclusion: A conjunction may contain a dominant planet, a supporting planet or a mixed partnership.

blocks.text: Combustion occurs when a planet comes very close to the Sun. The planet may find it harder to express independently because solar brilliance overwhelms its visibility and modifies its functioning. This does not mean the planet disappears from the chart or loses every result.

blocks.altText: A simple monochrome diagram showing the Sun, a nearby planet within a combustion zone and another planet farther away.
blocks.caption: Closer proximity to the Sun may increase combustion intensity.
blocks.purpose: Show combustion as a proximity-based condition rather than a simple on-off label.

items: Identify the planet near the Sun.
Measure the degree distance from the Sun.
Use the selected calculation standard for that planet's combustion limit.
Check the planet's sign dignity and house placement.
Check whether the planet owns important houses.
Check aspects, conjunctions and Dasha activation.
Describe the result as modified, pressured or internalised rather than completely absent.

blocks.title: Combustion limits require one defined standard
blocks.text: Different texts and software may use different limits, especially for Mercury and Venus. HoraLife should store the chosen calculation standard explicitly.

Retrogression is the apparent backward movement of a planet as observed from Earth. The planet does not literally reverse its orbit. In interpretation, retrogression may increase emphasis, repetition, reconsideration, internalisation or unusual expression, but its result depends on the full chart.

blocks.altText: A simple Earth-centred diagram showing a planet's normal apparent path and a temporary retrograde loop.
blocks.caption: Retrograde motion is an apparent observational effect.
blocks.purpose: Explain retrogression visually without implying literal backward orbit.

right.label: Safer reading
points: Check Dasha and the life area involved.

blocks.caption: Condition-combination checklist
rows: Planets involved, house, sign and degree distance
Distance from Sun and selected combustion standard
Whether retrograde and how the planet's expression changes
Own, exalted, friendly, neutral, enemy or debilitated sign
Support and pressure received or given
blocks.note: These conditions modify one another. None should be read in isolation.

blocks.title: Combust and retrograde planet in conjunction
blocks.scenario: A retrograde planet is closely conjunct the Sun and another planet.
steps: Record all planets, signs, houses and exact degrees.
Measure the planet's distance from the Sun.
Confirm whether it meets the chosen combustion limit.
Record its retrograde status.
Assess dignity, lordship and aspects.
Check which planet is activated by Dasha.
State the evidence as layered modifiers rather than one dramatic label.
blocks.conclusion: Multiple conditions require a layered judgement, not multiplied fear.

items: Record every planet's sign, house and exact degree.
Identify conjunctions by sign and house.
Measure degree distance between conjunct planets.
Check whether one planet appears dominant through multiple factors.
Measure each planet's distance from the Sun.
Apply one clearly defined combustion standard.
Record retrograde status without assigning an automatic result.
Check dignity, functional lordship, aspects and house relevance.
Check Dasha activation and the life area being studied.
Write supportive, pressure and mixed factors separately before concluding.

blocks.title: Foundation-level observation
blocks.scenario: Mercury is close to the Sun, retrograde and conjunct Venus.
steps: Record Mercury, Sun and Venus degrees.
Measure Mercury's distance from the Sun and Venus.
Check Mercury's sign dignity and house.
Identify Mercury's house lordships for the Lagna.
Check Venus's role and the relationship between Mercury and Venus.
Check aspects and Dasha activation.
Describe communication, analysis or decision-making as modified only if the full evidence supports it.
blocks.conclusion: The correct output is an evidence-based observation, not a fixed one-line prediction.

blocks.title: Conditions modify promise
blocks.text: Conjunction, combustion and retrogression influence how a planet delivers results. They do not replace the natal promise, house lordship, strength and timing analysis.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating all planets in the same sign as equally close.
commonMistakes.whyItIsWrong: Degree distance can make one conjunction much more intense than another.
commonMistakes.correctUnderstanding: Always record exact degrees and separation.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming a conjunction automatically creates a Yoga or Dosha.
commonMistakes.whyItIsWrong: Yoga and Dosha require specific conditions, strength and relevance.
commonMistakes.correctUnderstanding: Test the exact rule before naming it.

commonMistakes.whyItIsWrong: Combustion modifies expression but does not erase lordship, placement, dignity or all results.
commonMistakes.correctUnderstanding: Use combustion as one condition modifier.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using different combustion limits without documenting the standard.
commonMistakes.whyItIsWrong: Different standards may produce inconsistent results.
commonMistakes.correctUnderstanding: Choose and store one calculation standard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling every retrograde planet weak or harmful.
commonMistakes.whyItIsWrong: Retrogression may produce emphasis, repetition, internalisation or unusual expression depending on the chart.
commonMistakes.correctUnderstanding: Judge dignity, lordship, aspects and timing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Multiplying fear when several conditions occur together.
commonMistakes.whyItIsWrong: Multiple conditions require layered analysis, not dramatic language.
commonMistakes.correctUnderstanding: Separate evidence and assess the net result.

practicalExercise.title: Analyse Three Planetary Conditions
instructions: Create a sample sign containing the Sun and two other planets.
Assign exact degrees to all three planets.
Calculate the degree distance between the two non-solar planets.
Calculate each planet's distance from the Sun.
Record conjunction, possible combustion and retrograde status separately.
Add dignity, house lordship and aspects for each planet.
Write supportive, pressure and mixed observations without making a final prediction.
practicalExercise.expectedOutcome: The student can distinguish conjunction intensity, combustion proximity and retrograde status, and combine them with dignity, lordship, aspects and timing in a structured observation.

sessionSummary: A conjunction occurs when planets share the same sign or house.
Degree distance changes the intensity of planetary interaction.
Planets in conjunction retain their individual nature and lordship.
Dominance within a conjunction must be supported by multiple factors.
Combustion is based on proximity to the Sun.
A combust planet is modified, not automatically powerless.
Combustion limits must follow one clearly defined standard.
Retrogression is apparent backward motion viewed from Earth.
A retrograde planet is not automatically weak, strong or negative.
Conjunction, combustion and retrogression are condition modifiers.
Dignity, lordship, aspects, house relevance and Dasha remain essential.
Layered conditions require layered evidence, not fear-based conclusions.

questions.question: What most directly changes the intensity of a conjunction?
questions.explanation: Closer degree separation usually creates stronger direct interaction.

questions.question: What is combustion primarily based on?
questions.explanation: Combustion is assessed through the planet's proximity to the Sun.

questions.question: What is retrograde motion?
questions.explanation: Retrogression is an observational effect caused by relative movement.

questions.question: Which is the safest statement about a combust planet?
questions.explanation: Combustion is a modifier and must be combined with the full chart.

questions.question: All planets in the same sign interact with equal intensity.
questions.explanation: Degree distance and planetary condition change conjunction intensity.

questions.question: Every retrograde planet should be interpreted as weak.
questions.explanation: Retrogression modifies expression and must be judged with dignity, lordship and timing.

questions.question: Which factors should be checked before calling one planet dominant in a conjunction?
questions.answer: Dignity, functional lordship, degree closeness, natural strength, combustion, aspects and Dasha activation.
questions.explanation: Dominance should be supported by several chart factors.

questions.question: Why should conjunction, combustion and retrogression not be read in isolation?
questions.answer: Because they modify planetary expression, while the complete result also depends on dignity, lordship, house placement, aspects, natal promise and Dasha timing.
questions.explanation: These are layered conditions within the full chart.

contentReview.reviewNotes: The session separates conjunction, combustion and retrogression and treats each as a condition modifier rather than an isolated verdict. Exact combustion thresholds are intentionally not hard-coded because the product must first select and document one calculation standard. Human Jyotish SME review and source verification are required before publication.
